escena: SCENE (server room at night, Santiago): a work chart is PROJECTED onto her and onto the rough concrete wall — the concrete grain reads straight through the projected image and the chart's rows bend across her shoulder and chest. She stands inside the beam in a navy piqué polo, almost frontal, only her eyes turned down-left to where the projection falls on her — she has just stepped into the beam and stopped, mid-step, the sheet in her hand still half-raised; one column of that chart is empty and it is the empty column that lands on her chest. The projector sits LOW, at knee height, so its beam and the whole projected chart stay inside the action area of the frame. A glowing cool blue display on a rack beside her adds a second, softer light, also low. Very high contrast: her lit side burns, the other falls to near black. The whole frame is COOL and contemporary: daylight-neutral white balance, blue-leaning shadows, nothing warm, amber, golden or tungsten anywhere, no retro glow — the ONLY warm colour in the entire picture is the small orange sculpture itself. Everything except the sculpture is completely unbranded and no text is readable: the projected rows read as structure, never as words. A small orange sculpture sits on a low shelf at the right, inside the beam. CRITICAL FRAMING (square 1:1): the ACTION AREA is the lower 58% of the frame. The TOP 42% of the frame is one single dark, evenly toned surface with NOTHING in it: no object, no screen, no lamp, no window, no light beam, no bright spot, no shadow edge. If a person is in the picture, the top of her head is no higher than 42% down from the top edge. All action, all light and every bright patch stay inside the action area. REFRAMING (essential): the camera is further back, so she is framed SMALLER and LOWER in the square: the top of her head sits at the MIDDLE of the frame, 50% down from the top edge, and the whole upper half above her is dark and empty. The projected chart starts BELOW her shoulders' height and never climbs into the upper part of the frame.
